did_you_know.text: Did you know? David did not act alone: he consulted with the commanders of thousands, the commanders of hundreds, and all the leaders before proposing that the Ark of God be brought.
Did you know? David noted that Israel had not sought the Ark of God during Saul’s reign and asked to renew the nation’s connection with it.
Did you know? David gathered Israel from the Shihor in Egypt to the entrance of Hamath—a description of the very broad boundaries of the land and the people who assembled.
Did you know? The Ark was brought from Kiriath-jearim, and it is described as the Ark of God, which is called by the name of the LORD who is enthroned above the cherubim.
Did you know? The Ark was placed on a new cart, which Uzzah and his brother Ahio drove.
Did you know? The Ark’s journey was accompanied by a musical celebration featuring lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
Did you know? When the oxen stumbled at the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzzah reached out his hand to steady the Ark.
Did you know? Following Uzzah’s death, David named the place Perez-uzzah, and according to the text, the name remained until the time when the book’s author wrote.
Did you know? The Ark remained in the house of Obed-edom for three months, and during that time the LORD blessed Obed-edom and everything he owned.
